nodes.label: Bounded Persistent Read-Through Cache
nodes.rationale: Keyed by node plus exact file revision; namespaces bind the authenticated certificate fingerprint, persisted server epoch, and username so cached data can never cross an identity or authorization boundary. Payloads are SHA-256 checked, atomically written, owner-private, and LRU-evicted under a hard byte budget.

nodes.label: Process-Local Hot Range Tier
nodes.rationale: A bounded 256 MiB tier keeps a cold persistent block in memory after one integrity check so later small FUSE reads slice it locally instead of rereading and rehashing the whole block.

nodes.label: Adaptive Sequential Read-Ahead
nodes.rationale: macFUSE issues sequential access as independent read callbacks, so only one range request is ever in flight and a high-latency link sits idle. A speculative window scheduled ahead of the consumer, sharing the revision-keyed single-flight gate with demand reads, keeps the pipe full; a mutation bumps the file revision and orphans speculative blocks so read-after-write coherence holds.

nodes.label: Multiple Sequential Streams Per Handle
nodes.rationale: macOS multiplexes independent readers (player page-ins, Spotlight, Quick Look) over one FUSE fh. Tracking up to four streams per handle with LRU slot recycling stops one reader's seeks from destroying another's window; the earlier single-stream design zeroed the window dozens of times per minute during video playback.

nodes.label: Stall-Driven Window Sizing
nodes.rationale: The window doubles only when a demand read actually blocked >=10 ms on the network (direct evidence the window is under the bandwidth-delay product), at most once per half-window of delivered bytes, and holds while reads are prefetch hits. An earlier throughput hill-climber whipsawed between one and four blocks because throughput measured over demand-blocked time is pure noise once reads become cache hits. Bounded by --read-ahead-max-bytes (64 MiB default).

nodes.label: Cold-Start Read-Ahead Priming
nodes.rationale: Arming the window only after two in-order reads, at one block, left a freshly opened file with a serial cold ramp that stalled paced playback 150 ms-1 s (≈1 s under a concurrent Finder crawl). The first read of a handle now primes shallow speculation and a confirmed run arms several blocks deep; priming is gated on there being no tracked stream so mid-file seeks and thumbnail crawls do not waste read-ahead. Measured stalls drop to zero with per-read latency under ~75 ms.

nodes.label: Buffer Depth Is Not Fetch Concurrency
nodes.rationale: Fetching a whole window at once runs the link as a convoy: QUIC fair-shares bandwidth so each block completes in in-flight-bytes/link-rate and a demand miss waits that long (64 x 1 MiB in flight gave 1-3.5 s fetches and frozen playback). Speculation is bounded by a 32 MiB global in-flight byte pool (64 KiB units), a global cap of 8 concurrent speculative fetches, and a per-read burst of 8 blocks. The byte pool is the convoy ceiling, deliberately decoupled from --read-ahead-max-bytes, because with 8 MiB blocks the 8-fetch cap alone would put 64 MiB on the wire (playback demand spiked to ~700 ms; capping at 32 MiB dropped it to ~130 ms). Budgets use non-blocking try_acquire so an unaffordable block is unscheduled rather than parked, since a parked fetch counts as in-flight and leaves a never-fetched hole. Each speculative fetch carries a 120 s deadline; demand reads never take permits.

nodes.label: macOS Kernel Read-Ahead Disabled (-o noreadahead)
nodes.rationale: The macOS kernel's speculative read machinery is tuned for microsecond-latency local disks and is harmful on a network filesystem: it raced 100+ MB ahead of a paced consumer in 16 KiB page-ins, had those pages evicted, and re-read the same regions in multi-hundred-megabyte sweeps (5.5x read amplification) while the player's page-in queued 2-4 s behind. Disabling it volume-wide and delegating pipelining to the client prefetcher gave zero stalls in 60 s paced playback and roughly doubled cold sequential throughput (26.8 -> 49.8 MB/s). The page cache and mmap remain enabled.

nodes.label: Persistent Write-Behind Group Commit
nodes.rationale: Rewriting the whole manifest per mutation is O(total entries) under the state mutex every lookup needs; with tens of thousands of entries a read-ahead plus thumbnail burst floods the single writer thread with hours of backlog and the filesystem appears hung while the network is idle. The writer now drains batches of 256 jobs and writes the manifest once per batch, removing obsolete payloads only after that write to preserve manifest-first crash ordering; enqueue_and_wait still completes only after its batch flush so completion implies durability.

nodes.label: Cheap Content-Addressed Stores
nodes.rationale: Payload hashing and the atomic payload write happen before the state lock (file names are content-addressed, so this is concurrency-safe), and a store whose manifest entry is already current skips the clone and commit entirely.

nodes.label: Cache Writer Backpressure
nodes.rationale: Opportunistic read-through stores are dropped past 1,024 queued jobs or 128 MiB of queued range payloads (the in-memory tiers still serve them) so queue latency and memory stay bounded; coherence-critical invalidations and waited inserts are never dropped.

nodes.label: Node-Wide Directory Snapshot Invalidation
nodes.rationale: An enriched directory snapshot embeds each child's metadata, so any content/attribute/xattr/link/rename/exchange/remove must invalidate every cached snapshot containing that node, committed in one manifest transaction. Metadata is retained for the same 30-second lifetime as the snapshot so a second callback wave cannot degrade into one GetMetadata per child.

nodes.label: Fail-Closed Offline Writes
nodes.rationale: Mutating while disconnected would create merge risk: two clients editing overlapping ranges, racing renames/deletes, pathname reuse, or both believing they hold an exclusive lock, while the server may revoke access, change quota, or start a new export epoch. A safe design needs a durable idempotent mutation journal, base revisions and preconditions, stable object identity, reauthentication with permission/quota/lock revalidation, defined conflict rules, and user-visible reconciliation. Until then writes fail closed. This is deliberately an SMB-like read/page cache, not a synchronization product.

nodes.label: No Cold-Start Offline Mount
nodes.rationale: Without contacting the server a client cannot authenticate the current server identity and account, confirm the export epoch, learn that permissions were not revoked, or prove its cached namespace is current. Serving cached data only after a previously authenticated online mount disconnects keeps stale entries from becoming an unauthenticated substitute filesystem.
